title: dira check --json
description: The machine-readable verdict of `dira check`. This is a published contract: a pre-commit hook, a CI step or a coding agent parses it to decide whether a plan contradicts something the ledger already settled. The exit code is the primary signal (0 compliant, 2 at least one cited conflict, 1 dira's own error) and is repeated here so a caller holding only stdout still knows what it is looking at. Two rules below are security rules rather than shape rules, and are expressed as schema constraints so that a leak fails validation rather than review: a private entry is cited by reference and never by text (cst-0003), and no basis other than an alternative may carry a revisit condition, because entry.schema.json gives `revisit_if` only to `$defs/alternative` (docs/design.md §7).

plan.description: The candidate text that was checked, as it was given.

verdict.description: Whether the plan contradicts anything the ledger enforces.

exit_code.description: The process exit code this verdict produced. 1 is dira's own failure and never appears in a document, because a run that failed produced no verdict to serialise.

enforced_entries.description: How many entries were eligible to be cited. Reported because "no conflict" against a ledger the check failed to read is indistinguishable from "no conflict" against one it read in full, and only one of those is an answer.

conflicts.description: The citations, strongest first and then by entry id. The order is total, so two runs over the same ledger produce the same document.

notices.description: Matches against thinking this ledger has retired, redirected to whatever replaced it. Informational and never a verdict: a notice cannot change `verdict` or `exit_code`, because the entry it came from is superseded and a superseded entry enforces nothing. It exists so supersession moves enforcement rather than silently dropping it — a plan that would have been refused before gets told where the thinking went instead of a bare compliant verdict.

parents.description: What became of each parent ledger this one declares, in declared order, and empty for a ledger that declares none. It is how a caller tells a verdict reached over the whole enforcement set from one reached over part of it: a check that silently dropped a parent's constraints produces the same conflicts as a check that had none to drop, and only one of those is the whole answer. Never a verdict — a parent that could not be read does not move `verdict` or `exit_code` in either direction, because exit 2 means a cited conflict and nothing else. Optional: a document without it is one produced before this block existed, which is not the same fact as a ledger with no parents.

ref.description: An entry reference, optionally namespaced by a ledger name. Matches the `$defs/ref` pattern in entry.schema.json.

parent.description: One declared parent ledger's outcome. The three properties are the whole of what may be published about a parent, and `additionalProperties: false` is the enforcement rather than the documentation of that: a declaration also carries a filesystem path and may carry a `label`, dec-0011 says a private parent's label must never ship, and a path to that ledger identifies it at least as well as its label does. A document that carried either would fail validation here rather than be caught in review — which is the standard cst-0003 asks for, since a private strategic note in a public repository's history cannot be un-published.

namespace.description: The key the parent is declared under in this ledger's `[parents]`, and the namespace a ref like `me:cst-0002` resolves through (dec-0011). It is this ledger's own word for that parent, not the parent's `[ledger].name` — the two can disagree, and the declared key is what resolves. Same pattern as the namespace half of `$defs/ref`, so a citation built from it is a valid reference.

status.description: What became of this parent. `resolved`: it was read, and `evaluated` is a real count of what it contributed. `unresolved`: it is declared and could not be read from here. `withheld`: it is declared `visibility = "private"` and could not be read from here — a designed state and not a fault (dec-0018), because a private parent is expected to be absent wherever it has not been shared. The last two are the same unreadable ledger and are reported as different facts on purpose: one is a gap and one is the configuration working.

evaluated.description: How many of this parent's entries produced enforcement units. Note what is deliberately not here: a total. How many constraints a ledger nobody could open holds is not knowable from a run that could not open it, so this document states the count it can know and never one it would have had to invent.

allOf.description: A parent that could not be read evaluated none of its constraints. This is the honesty rule as a shape rule: without it a document could report a withheld parent alongside a count of what it supposedly holds, which is the one number such a run cannot have.

notice.description: One redirect. It names the entry that replaced the retired one and deliberately does not name the retired one itself: the replacement is what is enforced now, what carries the `supersedes` edge back, and what `dira why` should be pointed at, so it is the only id in the line worth acting on.

superseded_by.description: The entry recorded as having replaced the one the plan matched. Null where the record names none — a state flipped to `superseded` with no `supersedes` edge pointing at it, which is a broken record rather than a successor this document may invent.

replacement_enforced.description: Whether that replacement is itself enforcement substrate. False for a replacement that is staged, superseded in its turn, or of a kind the check never matches — and false always where there is none. A redirect that claimed otherwise would send a caller to an entry that will not stop them either.

basis.description: What inside the retired entry was matched, on the same vocabulary a citation uses.

score.description: The overlap that produced the notice, rounded to three decimals. Advisory, on the same footing as a conflict's score.

allOf.description: A replacement that does not exist cannot be enforced.

kind.description: The kinds that are enforcement substrate. An intent, a question and a note are never matched independently.

state.description: The enforced states. A staged decision is an unconfirmed regex-tier guess and is never cited (dec-0003); a superseded entry is not enforced here.

date.description: When the entry last changed, or when it was created if it has not. Absent only for an entry whose record carries no usable timestamp.

private.description: True when the entry is cited by reference only. The rule is unconditional rather than context-dependent: the binary cannot classify its own stdout, because a pipe into a pull-request body looks exactly like a terminal.

basis.description: What inside the entry was matched: a road the decision did not take, a rejected decision's own subject, or a standing rule.

rejected_alternative.description: The `alternatives[].option` text the plan proposes again.

why_not.description: That alternative's recorded reason, whitespace-collapsed out of its YAML folded scalar.

revisit_if.description: The condition under which the door legitimately reopens. Null means none is recorded — and for a constraint or a rejected decision's own subject it is null always, because that kind has no field to carry one. Null is never "never": `supersede` is the remedy that always exists.

supersede.description: The entry to supersede, in writing, to change what is enforced. Always the cited entry.

score.description: The overlap that produced the citation, rounded to three decimals. Advisory: the verdict is already decided by the time a conflict exists, and this number moves whenever the matcher is retuned. Do not branch on it.

allOf.description: cst-0003: a private entry is cited by ref and never by text, in every mode including this one.
Only an alternative can carry a revisit condition or an option text.
A non-private alternative citation must quote what was proposed and why it was refused. A citation with neither is an assertion.
